proposed_widenings.name: area_ward
proposed_widenings.justification: Forbiddance combines two mechanically distinct layers that no existing family captures: (1) an always-on persistent prohibition on magical travel into/through the warded area, and (2) event-triggered damage to creature-type-filtered creatures on enter/end-of-turn. The closest family, anchored_trigger, is architecturally restricted to event-driven notification signals (caller-owned). The travel prohibition is not event-driven at all — it is a permanent area property while the spell persists. A new 'area_ward' family is required that can express both a persistent area prohibition and a conditional, creature-typed damage rider.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You create a ward against magical travel that protects up to 40,000 square feet of floor space... creatures can't teleport into the area or use portals... the creature takes 5d10 Radiant or Necrotic damage (your choice when you cast this spell).

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredEvent.ends_turn_in_area
proposed_widenings.justification: The damage fires both on entry AND when a creature ends its turn in the area. anchored_trigger only has physical_contact and enters_area. This variant is needed even if anchored_trigger is not the right family for Forbiddance, as it will recur for other area-persistent damage spells.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When a creature of a chosen type enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there, the creature takes 5d10 Radiant or Necrotic damage.

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredFilter.creature_type_whitelist
proposed_widenings.justification: Forbiddance's damage applies only to creature types the caster designates at cast time (Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, Undead). The existing AnchoredFilter only supports creature_exemption_list (individual creature identity exemption). A creature-type whitelist is a categorically different filter — it operates on creature kind, not creature identity.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Choose one or more of the following: Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, and Undead.

proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredFilter.password_exemption
proposed_widenings.justification: Creatures that speak a designated password as they enter are immune to the damage. This is a runtime speech-check exemption, distinct from identity-based creature exemption lists.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can designate a password when you cast the spell. A creature that speaks the password as it enters the area takes no damage from the spell.

proposed_widenings.name: AreaWardEffect.block_travel
proposed_widenings.justification: The primary spell effect — prohibiting teleportation, portals, and planar travel into/through the area — is a persistent area prohibition with no representation in any existing surface type. The v4 atom block_travel exists, but no surface mechanism can attach it as an always-on ward property rather than a triggered signal.
proposed_widenings.evidence: creatures can't teleport into the area or use portals... The spell proofs the area against planar travel, and therefore prevents creatures from accessing the area by way of the Astral Plane, the Ethereal Plane, the Feywild, the Shadowfell, or the Plane Shift spell.

notes: Forbiddance is structurally a dual-layer area ward: one layer is an always-on prohibition (block_travel), the other is a conditional per-turn damage rider filtered by creature type. The anchored_trigger family is the nearest analogue but was designed for notification/signal spells (Alarm). Its 'signals' field is architecturally caller-owned (ARCHITECTURE.md) and cannot honestly host deterministic combat damage. A new 'area_ward' family is the minimal honest solution, requiring: persistent area prohibition effects, creature-type filtering at cast time, password exemption, and both enter-area and end-of-turn-in-area event triggers. The 10-minute ritual casting time maps cleanly to the existing CastingTime minutes variant. The 'day'-duration timed spell maps to the existing Duration.timed type with unit='day'.
